title: Carboplatin and vinorelbine · lung cancer
purpose: This chemotherapy aims to control lung cancer and symptoms when cisplatin is unsuitable. The team reviews benefit, side effects and your priorities.

agents.name: Vinorelbine
agents.mechanism: Disrupts microtubules needed for cell division
agents.explanation: Vinorelbine disrupts the cell structures that help divide chromosomes. This can slow cancer growth and also affect blood cells, nerves and the bowel.
agents.watch: Report fever, constipation, numbness or pain at the infusion site promptly.
risks: Low blood counts and serious infection

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: Carboplatin forms links in DNA that hinder copying and repair. Healthy tissues can also be harmed. Its dose depends on target exposure (AUC) and measured or estimated kidney function; AUC is not a fixed number of milligrams. There are two planned doses in this regimen.
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, nausea, hearing changes or numbness. Tell the nurse immediately about possible allergy during the infusion.

phases.label: Four 21 day cycles
phases.detail: Four 21 day cycles are planned, unless treatment stops or changes earlier. Day 1: carboplatin plus vinorelbine. Day 8: vinorelbine only. Your prescription specifies vinorelbine by drip OR capsules; these are alternatives, not extra doses.

phases.label: Review after treatment
phases.detail: Four cycles take about 12 weeks without delays. Your team agrees response scans and what happens next. Surgery or radiotherapy is not automatically included.

timeline.label: Symptom awareness
timeline.text: Symptoms may occur on any day; this is not a personal risk curve.

day_groups.title: Carboplatin + vinorelbine
day_groups.body: Both medicines after safety checks; confirm prescribed vinorelbine route.
day_groups.action: Your team confirms whether this dose can proceed.

day_groups.title: At home
day_groups.body: No planned chemotherapy on these days. Use only the support medicines prescribed for today.
day_groups.action: Call using your contact plan if unwell; do not wait for a treatment day.

day_groups.title: Vinorelbine only
day_groups.body: No carboplatin today. Vinorelbine by the prescribed route after safety checks.
day_groups.action: Your team confirms whether this dose can proceed.

day_groups.title: At home
day_groups.body: No planned chemotherapy on these days. Use only the support medicines prescribed for today.
day_groups.action: Call using your contact plan if unwell; do not wait for a treatment day.

support.title: Different support on Day 1 and Day 8
support.text: Day 1 carboplatin needs a stronger anti-sickness plan. Day 8 depends on whether vinorelbine is by drip or capsules. Use the written prescription for that day and route; do not repeat the entire Day 1course automatically.

support.title: Bowel plan
support.text: Vinorelbine and some anti-sickness medicines can cause constipation. Follow the prescribed bowel plan and call for severe tummy pain, swelling or vomiting.

support.title: If capsules are prescribed
support.text: Swallow whole with water and some food. Do not chew or open capsules. Do not take an extra dose after vomiting; contact the team for missed-dose advice. Return damaged capsules to pharmacy.

support.title: Check medicine interactions
support.text: The team should check all medicines, including anti-sickness treatment. Do not start new tablets, supplements or vaccines without advice.

questions.q: Am I having both oral and IV vinorelbine?
questions.a: No. Your written plan must identify the prescribed route for each dose. Do not treat capsule instructions as additional treatment.
Only vinorelbine is planned. Blood results, symptoms and the route determine whether dosing and the support plan are appropriate.
Ask your team to update the cycle record, prescription and contact plan. A stamp is not permission for the next dose.

context_label: Advanced/recurrent NSCLC when cisplatin is unsuitable
indication_text: NCCP 00614a: locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic NSCLC in patients unsuitable for cisplatin.
schedule_summary: Four 21 day cycles are planned, unless treatment stops or changes earlier. Day 1: carboplatin plus vinorelbine. Day 8: vinorelbine only. Your prescription specifies vinorelbine by drip OR capsules; these are alternatives, not extra doses.
administration_text: IV vinorelbine is usually 25 mg/m² over 15 minutes with a saline flush. Carboplatin AUC 5 is infused over 30 minutes on Day 1. Alternatively, the consultant may prescribe oral vinorelbine 60 mg/m² (maximum 120 mg) on Days 1/8 and consider 80 mg/m² from cycle 2 or 3 if tolerated. Do not convert doses or switch route yourself.
monitoring_summary: Before treatment: blood count, kidney/liver tests, nerve assessment and measured GFR where feasible or verified estimate. Before each cycle: blood count, kidneys/liver and nerves. Vinorelbine product information adds a blood count for each administration, including Day 8.
urgent_extra: Contact oncology immediately for fever, shaking chills, sudden illness, breathing difficulty, chest pain, bleeding, uncontrolled vomiting or severe constipation with tummy pain. Report new numbness or weakness before the next dose. Tell staff immediately about infusion pain or swelling.
consent_support: Discuss serious infection and low blood counts, allergy, constipation/ileus, neuropathy that can persist, mouth sores, extravasation if IV, oral-handling issues if capsules, fertility and individual material risks.

chronology_notes.title: Timing varies
chronology_notes.text: Tiredness, bowel changes and infection can occur between visits. Blood tests and your symptoms guide dose decisions; there is no guaranteed safe day.

chronology_notes.title: Changes to the plan
chronology_notes.text: The team may delay, omit or reduce doses for safety. Do not add a missed dose yourself.

timeline_note: Relative treatment days, without personal dates. Symptoms are not confined to a fixed day.
safety_note: Contact oncology immediately for fever, shaking chills, sudden illness, breathing difficulty, chest pain, bleeding, uncontrolled vomiting or severe constipation with tummy pain. Report new numbness or weakness before the next dose. Tell staff immediately about infusion pain or swelling.
passport_visit_note: Record actual treatment dates, route and delays. One completed-cycle stamp follows the final planned administration and team confirmation.
anatomy: Report new numbness, tingling or weakness before the next dose.
Report sores or pain that limits food or drink.
Breathing difficulty or swelling needs urgent help.
Severe constipation, pain, swelling or vomiting needs urgent advice.
Kidney tests guide dosing; report much less urine.
Call for fever or unusual bleeding; tell staff about infusion pain.

monitoring_schedule.title: My tests and checks
monitoring_schedule.note: Required safety checks are distinct from individual response imaging and follow-up. No routine tumour-marker interval is specified.

sections.title: Confirm the prescribed route
sections.text: Vinorelbine by drip and vinorelbine capsules are alternatives. Ask the team to mark your route.

sections.title: Day 1 and Day 8
sections.text: Day 1 includes carboplatin; Day 8 contains vinorelbine only. Arrange blood tests and clearance for each dose.

sections.title: Capsules only when prescribed
sections.text: Keep in the original packaging and follow pharmacy storage/handling instructions. Do not repeat a vomited dose or make up a missed dose.

evidence.intro: Carboplatin with vinorelbine has been studied in advanced lung cancer.
evidence.interpretation: Historical phase II evidence used alternating IV/oral vinorelbine, not every route variant, and cannot quantify comparative benefit.
